02.r: Introduces the comparison: the kingdom is like what happens in this story.
02.n: Greek puts the word first for emphasis: 'like is the kingdom'. The comparison is with the whole story that follows, not with the treasure alone (a reasonable reading).

03.r: Links the kingdom to the comparison.

04.r: Marks the particular kingdom Jesus proclaims.

05.r: God's royal rule, and the realm where it holds.
05.n: Abbott-Smith's first sense is abstract: 'sovereignty, royal power, dominion'. The YLT's 'reign' brings out that sense.

07.r: Matthew's way of naming God's kingdom.
07.n: Plural in the Greek. Abbott-Smith notes that the Septuagint uses this word chiefly for Hebrew שָׁמַיִם, hence the frequent plural. This study keeps 'the kingdom of the heavens' for Matthew's phrase.

08.r: A store of valuables someone had put away in the ground.

09.r: The treasure lies hidden in the field when the man finds it.
09.n: A perfect passive participle: it had been hidden and stayed hidden. Abbott-Smith notes the passive use in this verse.

11.r: A particular field in the story.
11.n: Greek has the article; several translations write 'a field'.

12.r: Farmland; he must buy it, so it is not yet his.

14.r: The man comes upon the treasure.
14.n: An aorist participle, literally 'having found', joined to 'hid'. Abbott-Smith notes that this verb is used of finding with or without a previous search; the story does not say he was looking.

16.r: He hides the treasure again before he can buy the field.
16.n: Abbott-Smith cites this verse for 'to hide, conceal' with an object. The BSB's 'again' is implied by the story, not written in the Greek.

17.r: Moves to what he does next.

18.r: His joy is the source of what he does.
18.n: The preposition means 'from'; here it gives the cause, as in 'for joy'.

19.r: Greek has the article with joy; English uses 'his'.

20.r: The man's gladness at what he has found.

21.r: Either the man's own joy or his joy over the treasure.
21.n: Literally 'of him' or 'of it': the pronoun could mean the man or the treasure. The KJV's 'joy thereof' takes it as joy over the treasure; the ASV, YLT and BSB read 'his joy'.

22.r: He leaves the field to raise the money.
22.n: Present tense, as are 'sells' and 'buys': the story is told as if happening now. The BSB turns all three into past tenses.

23.r: Joins the selling to the going.

24.r: He turns everything he owns into money.

26.n: Literally 'as many things as', stressing the whole amount; the YLT keeps 'as much as'.

29.r: He buys the field and with it the treasure.
29.n: Abbott-Smith notes the word's origin in the marketplace: 'to buy in the market, purchase'.

30.r: The article with field; English uses 'that' alone.

31.r: The field where the treasure lies.

32.r: Points back to the field where he found the treasure.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus opens the verse with Πάλιν, 'Again', which the KJV, Geneva and YLT render and the DRC, ASV and BSB do not. It also places 'sells' at a different point in the clause, likely after 'all that he has', as the YLT's 'all, as much as he hath, he selleth' suggests; the KJV's English is the same either way.
